words.gloss: than the companionship of such associates

literal: In the midst of battle, on the way, abandoning, like an untrained horse, those who are like—than their companionship, solitude is best.
translation: Solitude is far better than the companionship of those who, like an untrained horse, abandon their rider in the midst of battle.
modern: போர்க்களத்தின் நடுவே தன் மேல் ஏறியவனைத் தள்ளிவிட்டு ஓடும் பழக்கப்படாத குதிரையைப் போன்றவர்களின் நட்பை விட, தனியாக இருப்பதே மிகச் சிறந்தது.
explanation: This couplet warns us against unreliable and harmful friends by comparing them to an untrained horse (கல்லாமா). Just as a wild, untrained horse will panic and throw its rider off in the middle of a battle (அமரகத்து ஆற்றறுக்கும்), bad friends will desert you when you face critical danger or adversity. The poet emphasizes that being completely alone (தனிமை) is far superior (தலை) to having the companionship of such untrustworthy people (தமரின்). The vivid imagery of the battlefield highlights how dangerous it is to rely on false friends during times of crisis.
